title: Setting Up Dynamic DNS with No-IP
why: Most home internet connections have a dynamic IP address that changes periodically. This means the IP address you use to access your server from the internet may stop working after your ISP assigns you a new one. Dynamic DNS (DDNS) solves this by mapping a hostname (like myserver.ddns.net) to your current IP address and automatically updating it whenever it changes. No-IP is a popular free DDNS provider.

instructions.text: Create a free account at https://www.noip.com/. After registering, create a hostname (e.g. myserver.ddns.net) from the No-IP dashboard.
Install the No-IP Dynamic Update Client (DUC) on your server. First, download it.
instructions.command:
cd /usr/local/src
sudo wget https://www.noip.com/client/linux/noip-duc-linux.tar.gz
sudo tar xzf noip-duc-linux.tar.gz

cd noip-2.1.9-1
sudo make
sudo make install
instructions.note: During installation, you'll be prompted for your No-IP email and password, and asked to choose which hostname to update.

instructions.text: Create a systemd service so the No-IP client starts automatically on boot. Create the service file:
Add the following content to the service file:
instructions.command:
[Unit]
Description=No-IP Dynamic DNS Update Client
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=forking
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/noip2
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable noip2
sudo systemctl start noip2

instructions.note: You should see 'active (running)'. The client will now automatically update your No-IP hostname with your current public IP.

instructions.text: Test your setup by accessing your server using your No-IP hostname from outside your network.
instructions.note: Replace myserver.ddns.net with your actual hostname. You should see the Nginx default page.

instructions.text: Optionally, update your Nginx server configuration to use your hostname.
instructions.note: Add this to your Nginx server block and reload Nginx.

questions.text: Why do you need Dynamic DNS for a home server?
options: Because most home internet connections have a dynamic IP that changes, and DDNS keeps your hostname pointed at the current IP
To encrypt traffic between your server and the internet
Because DNS is required for Nginx to work

questions.text: What does the No-IP DUC (Dynamic Update Client) do?
options: It provides a firewall for your server
It monitors your public IP and updates the No-IP DNS record when it changes
It replaces your router's DNS settings
It assigns a static IP to your server

questions.text: Why should you create a systemd service for the No-IP client?
options: Systemd makes the client run faster
So the client starts automatically on boot and restarts if it crashes
Systemd is required for all Linux applications
To allow the client to modify firewall rules
